title: TRINITY ESALC-I GVPT2 and IR with automatic Eckart gauge
summary: Preserve the frozen SMITH analytic metric and single-mode stencils, align every geometry to the reference Eckart frame, and require harmonic ESALC-I/ESALC-C frequency and IR identity.
gates: Frozen SMITH definition and ESALC-I chart have the same full-rank Wilson row space
Sparse B prime has no numerical fallback primitives at any stencil point
Fixed SMITH-to-ESALC-I row transform and Cartesian angstrom-to-bohr derivative conversion
Complete vibrational G double-prime from single-mode differences of analytic Wilson G prime
Only reference and plus/minus single-mode Cartesian Hessians and dipole samples
Fermi-only resonance polyads and second-order IR transition moments
Automatic mass-weighted Eckart alignment at every displaced ESALC-I geometry
Harmonic ESALC-I/ESALC-C frequencies and IR intensities from the same Cartesian Hessian and dipole Jacobian agree within numerical tolerance
coordinate_policy: Use one frozen full-rank ESALC-I chart and a matching SMITH definition. Map native SMITH B rows to the chart with a fixed reference transformation; construct B prime at each single-mode point and reject any numerical fallback. Orient every realization automatically in the reference Eckart frame.
backend_policy: KeyMaker authorizes Cartesian E/G/H and dipole providers; SMITH supplies the frozen Wilson definition and B, the resident sparse B-prime builder supplies analytic derivatives, and TRINITY constructs G prime, G double-prime, GVPT2 and IR intensities. Require the Cartesian harmonic reference to match both internal frequencies and IR intensities.
